$\eta(\cdot - y)$ and $u$, gives the first identity by \Cref{lem:schwartz-shift-reflect}. For
$k = 1$, apply \Cref{thm:convolution-adjoint} with the conjugate exponent $q$ of $p$ to both
sides; Schwartz functions lie in every $L_q$, and the two reflected convolutions differ by the
sign. Induction on $k$ gives the general case, with
$\partial_a \partial^w u = \partial^w \partial_a u$
(\Cref{lem:directional-derivatives-commute}).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Weak derivatives commute with convolution]
\label{thm:weak-derivative-convolution}
\lean{Rd.conv_eq_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp, Rd.conv_eq_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp_of_memLp,
  Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_conv, Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_toLp_conv}
\leanok
\uses{thm:weak-derivative-tempered, lem:distribution-transpose, lem:schwartz-shift-reflect,
  lem:conv-derivative-transfer, lem:weak-derivative-integral, lem:weak-derivative-basic,
  def:test-schwartz, thm:young}
For all $1 \leq p, r \leq \infty$, every $f \in L_p(V)$, every $g \in L_r(V)$ and every
$v \in V^k$ such that $g$ is the weak derivative $\partial^v f$ on $V$, every Schwartz
function $\eta$ and every $x \in V$,
\[
  (\eta * g)(x) = \bigl((\partial^v \eta) * f\bigr)(x) .
\]
For every $1 \leq p < \infty$, every $f \in L_p(V)$, every Schwartz function $\eta$ and every
$v \in V^k$, $(\partial^v \eta) * f$ is the weak derivative $\partial^v (\eta * f)$ on $V$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
Let $S_f$ and $S_g$ be the tempered distributions of $f$ and $g$, and for every Schwartz
function $\zeta$ let $\rho_x \zeta = \zeta(x - \cdot)$ be its reflected translate.
By \Cref{lem:schwartz-shift-reflect}, $(\eta * g)(x) = S_g(\rho_x \eta)$, which is
$\partial^v S_f(\rho_x \eta) = S_f\bigl((-1)^k \partial^v \rho_x \eta\bigr)$ by
\Cref{thm:weak-derivative-tempered} and \Cref{lem:distribution-transpose}. Again by
\Cref{lem:schwartz-shift-reflect}, $(-1)^k \partial^v \rho_x \eta = \rho_x(\partial^v \eta)$,
and $S_f\bigl(\rho_x(\partial^v \eta)\bigr) = ((\partial^v \eta) * f)(x)$.

For the second statement, $\eta * f$ and $(\partial^v \eta) * f$ lie in $L_p$ by
\Cref{thm:young}, so they are locally integrable. For every test function $\varphi$ on $V$,
\Cref{lem:conv-derivative-transfer} with the Schwartz function $u = \varphi$
(\Cref{def:test-schwartz}) is the identity of \Cref{lem:weak-derivative-integral}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Weak derivatives of convolutions in $L_p$]
\label{lem:weak-derivative-convolution-lp}
\lean{Rd.hasWeakLineDeriv_convLp}
\leanok
\uses{thm:weak-derivative-convolution, lem:conv-op}
For all $1 \leq p, r < \infty$, every $k$, all directions $v = (v_1, \dots, v_k) \in V^k$, every
Schwartz function $\eta$, every $f \in L_p(V)$ and every $g \in L_r(V)$ with $g = \partial^v f$
weakly on $V$, $\eta * g = \partial^v (\eta * f)$ weakly on $V$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The weak derivative of $\eta * f$ is $(\partial^v \eta) * f$, and $(\partial^v \eta) * f =
\eta * g$ at every point (\Cref{thm:weak-derivative-convolution}).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Weak derivatives and convolution on open sets]
\label{lem:weak-derivative-convolution-local}
\lean{Rd.coe_shiftReflect_eq_comp, Rd.hasCompactSupport_shiftReflect,
  Rd.tsupport_shiftReflect_subset, Rd.conv_eq_conv_iteratedLineDerivOp_of_hasWeakLineDeriv}
\leanok
\uses{lem:schwartz-shift-reflect, lem:weak-derivative-complex-test}
Let $\Omega \subseteq V$ be open, $v \in V^k$, $g = \partial^v f$ weakly on $\Omega$, $\eta$ a
Schwartz function with compact support and $x \in V$ with $x - y \in \Omega$ for every $y$ in the
support of $\eta$. Then $(\eta * g)(x) = ((\partial^v \eta) * f)(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The reflected translate $\rho_x \eta = \eta(x - \cdot)$ has compact support in $\Omega$, so
\Cref{lem:weak-derivative-complex-test} and \Cref{lem:schwartz-shift-reflect} give
$(\eta * g)(x) = \int \rho_x \eta \, g = (-1)^k \int (\partial^v \rho_x \eta) \, f
= \int \rho_x(\partial^v \eta) \, f = ((\partial^v \eta) * f)(x)$.
\end{proof}

\section{Plancherel bounds}
\label{sec:plancherel-bounds}

A family $(\theta_j)_{j \in \N}$ of integrable kernels on $V$ defines the analysis operator
$f \mapsto (\theta_j * f)_j$ and, for every finite set $s \subseteq \N$, the synthesis operator
$(g_j)_j \mapsto \sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j$. On $L_2(V)$ both are bounded by the Fourier
overlap alone: Plancherel's theorem and the convolution theorem on $L_2$ turn them into
multiplications by the functions $\widehat{\theta_j}$. Throughout, $T_K f = K * f$ is the
convolution operator of \Cref{lem:conv-op} on $L_2(V)$, and $\widehat f$ the Fourier transform
of $f \in L_2(V)$ of \Cref{sec:sobolev-two-littlewood-paley}.

\begin{lemma}[Cauchy--Schwarz and squares of $L_2$ norms]
\label{lem:l2-squares}
\lean{enorm_sum_mul_sq_le, Rd.lintegral_enorm_conv_sq_eq}
\leanok
\uses{lem:plancherel-l2, lem:conv-op}
For every seminormed ring $R$, such as $\C$, every finite set $s$ and all $a_j, b_j \in R$,
$j \in s$,
\[
  \Bigl\|\sum_{j \in s} a_j b_j\Bigr\|^2 \leq \Bigl(\sum_{j \in s} \|a_j\|^2\Bigr)
  \Bigl(\sum_{j \in s} \|b_j\|^2\Bigr).
\]
For every integrable $K$ on $V$ and every $f \in L_2(V)$,
$\int_V |(K * f)(x)|^2 \, dx = \|T_K f\|_2^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The inequality is the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for the norms (Mathlib's
\texttt{Finset.\allowbreak sum\_mul\_sq\_le\_sq\_mul\_sq}) after the triangle inequality and
$\|a b\| \leq \|a\| \, \|b\|$. The identity follows from \Cref{lem:plancherel-l2}, since
$T_K f = K * f$ almost everywhere (\Cref{lem:conv-op}).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The analysis bound on $L_2$]
\label{thm:l2-analysis-bound}
\lean{Rd.tsum_enorm_convLp_sq_le, Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_conv_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{thm:convolution-theorem-l2, lem:plancherel-l2, lem:l2-squares, lem:fourier-integrable,
  def:lq-norm}
For every $B \in [0, \infty]$, every family $(\theta_j)_{j \in \N}$ of integrable kernels on $V$
with $\sum_j |\widehat{\theta_j}(\xi)|^2 \leq B$ for almost every $\xi \in V$, and every
$f \in L_2(V)$,
\[
  \sum_j \|\theta_j * f\|_2^2 \leq B \, \|f\|_2^2 , \qquad
  \int_V \|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}^2 \, dx \leq B \int_V |f(x)|^2 \, dx .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
By \Cref{thm:convolution-theorem-l2} and monotone convergence,
\[
  \sum_j \|\theta_j * f\|_2^2
  = \int_V \Bigl(\sum_j |\widehat{\theta_j}(\xi)|^2\Bigr) |\widehat f(\xi)|^2 \, d\xi
  \leq B \int_V |\widehat f(\xi)|^2 \, d\xi = B \, \|f\|_2^2
\]
by \Cref{lem:plancherel-l2}; the integrand is measurable since every $\widehat{\theta_j}$ lies
in $L_\infty(V)$ (\Cref{lem:fourier-integrable}). The second inequality is the first for the
class of $f$, written with $\|a\|_{\ell_2}^2 = \sum_j a_j^2$ (\Cref{def:lq-norm}),
\Cref{lem:plancherel-l2}, \Cref{lem:l2-squares} and monotone convergence.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The Fourier transform of a sum of convolutions]
\label{lem:fourier-sum-conv}
\lean{Rd.fourier_sum_convLp}
\leanok
\uses{thm:convolution-theorem-l2}
For every family $(\theta_j)_{j \in \N}$ of integrable kernels on $V$, all $g_j \in L_2(V)$ and
every finite set $s \subseteq \N$,
$\mathcal F\bigl(\sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j\bigr)
= \sum_{j \in s} \widehat{\theta_j} \, \widehat{g_j}$ almost everywhere.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The Fourier transform on $L_2(V)$ is linear (Mathlib's
\texttt{Fourier\allowbreak Transform.\allowbreak fourier\_\allowbreak sum}); apply
\Cref{thm:convolution-theorem-l2} to each term.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The synthesis bound on $L_2$]
\label{thm:l2-synthesis-bound}
\lean{Rd.enorm_sum_convLp_sq_le, Rd.lintegral_enorm_sum_conv_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{lem:fourier-sum-conv, lem:l2-squares, lem:plancherel-l2, def:lq-norm}
For every $B \in [0, \infty]$, every family $(\theta_j)_{j \in \N}$ of integrable kernels on $V$
with $\sum_j |\widehat{\theta_j}(\xi)|^2 \leq B$ for almost every $\xi \in V$, all
$g_j \in L_2(V)$ and every finite set $s \subseteq \N$,
\[
  \Bigl\|\sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j\Bigr\|_2^2 \leq B \sum_{j \in s} \|g_j\|_2^2
\]
and
\[
  \int_V \Bigl|\sum_{j \in s} (\theta_j * g_j)(x)\Bigr|^2 \, dx
  \leq B \int_V \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}^2 \, dx .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
By \Cref{lem:fourier-sum-conv} and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality of \Cref{lem:l2-squares}, for
almost every $\xi$,
\[
  \Bigl|\mathcal F\Bigl(\sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j\Bigr)(\xi)\Bigr|^2
  \leq \Bigl(\sum_{j \in s} |\widehat{\theta_j}(\xi)|^2\Bigr)
  \sum_{j \in s} |\widehat{g_j}(\xi)|^2
  \leq B \sum_{j \in s} |\widehat{g_j}(\xi)|^2 .
\]
Integration and \Cref{lem:plancherel-l2} on both sides give the first inequality. The second is
the first for the classes of the $g_j$ (\Cref{lem:plancherel-l2}), with
$\sum_{j \in s} |g_j(x)|^2 \leq \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}^2$ (\Cref{def:lq-norm}).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Plancherel bounds for Calder\'on--Zygmund families]
\label{cor:cz-family-l2-bounds}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.tsum_enorm_convLp_sq_le, Rd.IsCZFamily.lintegral_lqNorm_conv_sq_le,
  Rd.IsCZFamily.enorm_sum_convLp_sq_le, Rd.IsCZFamily.lintegral_enorm_sum_conv_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{def:cz-family, thm:l2-analysis-bound, thm:l2-synthesis-bound}
For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$ and every Calder\'on--Zygmund family $(\theta_j)_{j \in \N}$ on
$V$ with overlap $B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$,
\[
  \sum_j \|\theta_j * f\|_2^2 \leq B \, \|f\|_2^2 , \qquad
  \int_V \|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}^2 \, dx \leq B \int_V |f(x)|^2 \, dx
\]
for every $f \in L_2(V)$, and
\[
  \Bigl\|\sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j\Bigr\|_2^2 \leq B \sum_{j \in s} \|g_j\|_2^2
\]
and
\[
  \int_V \Bigl|\sum_{j \in s} (\theta_j * g_j)(x)\Bigr|^2 \, dx
  \leq B \int_V \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}^2 \, dx
\]
for all $g_j \in L_2(V)$ and every finite set $s \subseteq \N$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The kernels of a Calder\'on--Zygmund family are integrable, and the overlap bound holds at
every $\xi$ (\Cref{def:cz-family}); apply \Cref{thm:l2-analysis-bound} and
\Cref{thm:l2-synthesis-bound}.
\end{proof}

\section{The signed Calder\'on--Zygmund decomposition}
\label{sec:calderon-zygmund-signed}

The Calder\'on--Zygmund decomposition of \Cref{thm:calderon-zygmund} selects the maximal big
cubes of a function $G : V \to [0, \infty]$ at a height $t$. This section splits a function
$f : V \to E$ with values in a real normed space $E$, such as $\C$, along these cubes into a
good part, which is $f$ outside the exceptional set $\Omega$ and the mean of $f$ on each maximal
big cube, and a bad part, which is a sum of pieces with mean zero, one on each cube. For
$G = \|f\|$ the good part is bounded by $2^n t$; for a family $(g_j)_j$ the cubes of
$G = \|(\|g_j\|)_j\|_{\ell_q}$ serve every $g_j$. The definitions and the bounds on the bad
pieces hold for the cubes of every $G$. The bounds on the good part follow from a comparison
with the nonnegative good part of \Cref{def:calderon-zygmund-good-part}, and those on the bad
pieces from the bound of the norm of a mean in \Cref{lem:norm-mean-square-bound}. As there,
$V$ has dimension $n$, and for a dyadic cube $Q$ and $f : V \to E$ the mean is
$f_Q = |Q|^{-1} \int_Q f$, the Bochner integral, which is $0$ when $f$ is not integrable on $Q$.
For scalar functions this is the decomposition of Calder\'on and
Zygmund~\cite{CalderonZygmund1952}; see also Stein's book~\cite{SteinSingular}. The Carleson
project
\cite{CarlesonBlueprint,CarlesonLean} has a scalar Calder\'on--Zygmund decomposition
on doubling metric measure spaces.

\begin{lemma}[Means of vector-valued functions]
\label{lem:norm-mean-square-bound}
\lean{MeasureTheory.enorm_average_le, MeasureTheory.measure_mul_enorm_setAverage_le,
  MeasureTheory.setLIntegral_enorm_sub_setAverage_le,
  MeasureTheory.measure_mul_lqNorm_setAverage_le,
  MeasureTheory.setLIntegral_lqNorm_sub_setAverage_le,
  MeasureTheory.lintegral_sq_le_mul_lintegral_of_ae_le}
\leanok
\uses{lem:lq-norm-means, lem:lq-basic, lem:calderon-zygmund-good-parts}
For every measure space $(X, \mu)$, every real normed space $E$ and every $f : X \to E$,
\[
  \Bigl\| \frac{1}{\mu(X)} \int f \, d\mu \Bigr\| \leq \frac{1}{\mu(X)} \int \|f\| \, d\mu
\]
in $[0, \infty]$. For every set $s \subseteq X$ with $\mu(s) < \infty$ and the mean
$f_s = \mu(s)^{-1} \int_s f \, d\mu$,
\[
  \mu(s) \, \|f_s\| \leq \int_s \|f\| \, d\mu ,
  \qquad
  \int_s \|f - f_s\| \, d\mu \leq 2 \int_s \|f\| \, d\mu .
\]
For every $1 \leq q \leq \infty$, every such $s$ and every countable family of functions
$g_i : X \to E$, $i \in I$, that are almost everywhere strongly measurable on $s$,
\[
  \mu(s) \, \|(\|(g_i)_s\|)_i\|_{\ell_q} \leq \int_s \|(\|g_i\|)_i\|_{\ell_q} \, d\mu
\]
and
\[
  \int_s \|(\|g_i - (g_i)_s\|)_i\|_{\ell_q} \, d\mu \leq 2 \int_s \|(\|g_i\|)_i\|_{\ell_q} \, d\mu .
\]
For every almost everywhere measurable $u : X \to [0, \infty]$ and every
$c \in [0, \infty]$ with $u \leq c$ almost everywhere, $\int u^2 \, d\mu \leq c \int u \, d\mu$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
Both means are integrals for the measure $\mu(X)^{-1} \mu$, and the norm of a Bochner integral
is at most the integral of the norm. On $s$ this gives
$\mu(s) \, \|f_s\| \leq \mu(s) \, \|f\|_s = \int_s \|f\|$, and with
$\|f - f_s\| \leq \|f\| + \|f_s\|$ also
$\int_s \|f - f_s\| \leq \int_s \|f\| + \mu(s) \, \|f_s\| \leq 2 \int_s \|f\|$. For the family,
$\|(\|(g_i)_s\|)_i\|_{\ell_q} \leq \|(\|g_i\|_s)_i\|_{\ell_q} \leq \|(\|g_i\|)_i\|_{\ell_q, s}$ by
\Cref{lem:lq-norm-means}, and Minkowski's inequality in $\ell_q$ (\Cref{lem:lq-basic}) replaces
the triangle inequality. The last statement is the case $r = 2$ of
\Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-good-parts}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Signed averages, good parts and bad pieces]
\label{def:calderon-zygmund-signed}
\lean{Rd.czAverageC, Rd.hasSum_czAverageC,
  Rd.stronglyMeasurable_czAverageC, Rd.czGoodC, Rd.aestronglyMeasurable_czGoodC, Rd.czBadC,
  Rd.czBadPart}
\leanok
\uses{def:calderon-zygmund-cubes, def:calderon-zygmund-good-part, thm:calderon-zygmund}
Let $E$ be a real normed space, $G : V \to [0, \infty]$, $t \in [0, \infty]$, and let $\Omega$
be the exceptional set of the maximal big cubes of $G$ at height $t$. For $f : V \to E$ the
signed averages, the good part and the bad part of $f$ are
\[
  A f = \sum_{Q \text{ maximal big}} f_Q \, \mathbf 1_Q ,
  \qquad
  \mathcal G f = \mathbf 1_{V \setminus \Omega} \, f + A f ,
  \qquad
  \mathcal B f = f - \mathcal G f ,
\]
and the bad piece of $f$ on a dyadic cube $Q$ is $b_Q f = \mathbf 1_Q \, (f - f_Q)$. The
series converges at every point, the function $A f$ is strongly measurable, and $\mathcal G f$
is almost everywhere strongly measurable if $f$ is.
\end{definition}

Every point lies in at most one maximal big cube (\Cref{thm:calderon-zygmund}), so at most one
term of the series is nonzero. For functions $h : V \to [0, \infty]$ the same formulas are
$A h$ and $\mathcal G h$ of \Cref{def:calderon-zygmund-good-part}; the signed versions are
compared with them through the norm.

\begin{lemma}[Signed averages and good parts]
\label{lem:calderon-zygmund-signed-good}
\lean{Rd.czAverageC_eq_of_mem, Rd.czAverageC_eq_zero_of_notMem, Rd.enorm_czAverageC_le,
  Rd.enorm_czGoodC_le, Rd.lintegral_enorm_czGoodC_le, Rd.integrable_czGoodC}
\leanok
\uses{def:calderon-zygmund-signed, lem:calderon-zygmund-averages, lem:norm-mean-square-bound,
  lem:calderon-zygmund-good-parts}
For every real normed space $E$, every $G : V \to [0, \infty]$, every $t \in [0, \infty]$ and
every $f : V \to E$:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $A f = f_Q$ on every maximal big cube $Q$, and $A f = 0$ outside $\Omega$;
  \item $\|A f(x)\| \leq A \|f\|(x)$ and $\|\mathcal G f(x)\| \leq \mathcal G \|f\|(x)$ for
    every $x \in V$;
  \item $\int \|\mathcal G f\| \leq \int \|f\|$, and $\mathcal G f$ is integrable if $f$ is.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
At a point of $\Omega$ only one term of $A f$ survives, and outside $\Omega$ none does. On a
maximal big cube $Q$, $\|f_Q\| \leq \|f\|_Q$ by \Cref{lem:norm-mean-square-bound}, which gives
the first bound, and the second follows with the triangle inequality. Integrating it,
$\int \|\mathcal G f\| \leq \int \mathcal G \|f\| = \int \|f\|$ by
\Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-good-parts}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Bounds of the signed good part]
\label{thm:calderon-zygmund-signed-good-bounds}
\lean{Rd.ae_enorm_czGoodC_le, Rd.lintegral_enorm_czGoodC_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{lem:calderon-zygmund-signed-good, lem:calderon-zygmund-good-parts,
  lem:norm-mean-square-bound}
Let $n \geq 1$. For every real normed space $E$, every integrable $f : V \to E$ and every
$t \in (0, \infty]$, the good part $\mathcal G f$ for the maximal big cubes of $\|f\|$ at
height $t$ satisfies
\[
  \|\mathcal G f(x)\| \leq 2^n t \quad \text{for almost every } x \in V, \qquad
  \int \|\mathcal G f\|^2 \leq 2^n t \int \|f\| .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
By \Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-signed-good}, $\|\mathcal G f\| \leq \mathcal G \|f\|$, which is
at most $2^n t$ almost everywhere by \Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-good-parts} with
$G' = \|f\|$. Then \Cref{lem:norm-mean-square-bound} gives
$\int \|\mathcal G f\|^2 \leq 2^n t \int \|\mathcal G f\| \leq 2^n t \int \|f\|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The bad part and its pieces]
\label{lem:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces}
\lean{Rd.czGoodC_add_czBadC, Rd.czBadPart_of_mem, Rd.czBadPart_of_notMem,
  Rd.czBadC_eq_zero_of_notMem, Rd.czBadC_eq_of_mem, Rd.hasSum_czBadPart, Rd.czBadC_eq_tsum,
  Rd.integrable_czBadPart, Rd.lintegral_enorm_czBadPart_le, Rd.integrable_czBadC,
  Rd.lintegral_enorm_czBadC_le}
\leanok
\uses{def:calderon-zygmund-signed, lem:calderon-zygmund-signed-good, lem:norm-mean-square-bound,
  lem:dyadic-cubes}
For every real normed space $E$, every $G : V \to [0, \infty]$, every $t \in [0, \infty]$ and
every $f : V \to E$:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $\mathcal G f + \mathcal B f = f$, $\mathcal B f = 0$ outside $\Omega$,
    $\mathcal B f = f - f_Q$ on every maximal big cube $Q$, and
    $\mathcal B f(x) = \sum_Q b_Q f(x)$ for every $x \in V$, the sum over the maximal big cubes,
    with at most one nonzero term;
  \item every dyadic cube $Q$ satisfies $\int \|b_Q f\| \leq 2 \int_Q \|f\|$, and $b_Q f$ is
    integrable if $f$ is integrable on $Q$;
  \item if $f$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable, then
    $\int \|\mathcal B f\| \leq 2 \int \|f\|$, and $\mathcal B f$ is integrable if $f$ is.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The identity $\mathcal G f + \mathcal B f = f$ is the definition of $\mathcal B f$, and the rest
of the first part follows from \Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-signed-good}. Since
$|Q| < \infty$ (\Cref{lem:dyadic-cubes}), \Cref{lem:norm-mean-square-bound} gives
$\int \|b_Q f\| = \int_Q \|f - f_Q\| \leq 2 \int_Q \|f\|$. Finally
$\|\mathcal B f\| \leq \|f\| + \|\mathcal G f\|$, and
\Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-signed-good} bounds the integral of the second term.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Mean zero and mass of the bad pieces]
\label{thm:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces-mean-mass}
\lean{Rd.integral_czBadPart, Rd.setIntegral_czBadC, Rd.tsum_lintegral_enorm_czBadPart_le}
\leanok
\uses{lem:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces, lem:calderon-zygmund-averages, lem:dyadic-cubes}
For every real normed space $E$, every $f : V \to E$ and every dyadic cube $Q$,
\[
  \int b_Q f = 0 ,
\]
and for every $G : V \to [0, \infty]$, every $t \in [0, \infty]$ and every maximal big cube
$Q$ of $G$ at height $t$, $\int_Q \mathcal B f = 0$. Moreover
\[
  \sum_{Q \text{ maximal big}} \int \|b_Q f\| \leq 2 \int \|f\| .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
If $f$ is integrable on $Q$, then $\int_Q (f - f_Q) = \int_Q f - |Q| \, f_Q = 0$ (Mathlib's
\texttt{setAverage\_\allowbreak sub\_\allowbreak setAverage}); otherwise $f - f_Q$ is not
integrable on $Q$ either, and both integrals are $0$ by convention, as they are for every
function when $E$ is not complete. On a maximal big cube,
$\mathcal B f = f - f_Q$ by \Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces}. By the same lemma,
$\int \|b_Q f\| \leq 2 \int_Q \|f\|$ for every maximal big cube $Q$, and
\Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-averages} sums these bounds to $2 \int \|f\|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The decomposition of a family]
\label{thm:calderon-zygmund-signed-family}
\lean{Rd.ae_lqNorm_czGoodC_le, Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGoodC_le, Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czGoodC_sq_le,
  Rd.lintegral_lqNorm_czBadPart_le, Rd.tsum_lintegral_lqNorm_czBadPart_le}
\leanok
\uses{lem:calderon-zygmund-signed-good, lem:calderon-zygmund-good-parts,
  lem:norm-mean-square-bound, lem:calderon-zygmund-averages, lem:dyadic-cubes}
Let $1 \leq q \leq \infty$, let $E$ be a real normed space, and let $g_j : V \to E$, $j \in \N$,
be almost everywhere strongly measurable, with $G(x) = \|(\|g_j(x)\|)_j\|_{\ell_q}$. For every
$G' : V \to [0, \infty]$ and every $t \in [0, \infty]$, with the good parts $\mathcal G g_j$ and
the maximal big cubes of $G'$ at height $t$,
\[
  \int \|(\|\mathcal G g_j(x)\|)_j\|_{\ell_q} \, dx \leq \int G ,
\]
every dyadic cube $Q$ satisfies
\[
  \int \|(\|b_Q g_j(x)\|)_j\|_{\ell_q} \, dx \leq 2 \int_Q G ,
\]
and
\[
  \sum_{Q \text{ maximal big}} \int \|(\|b_Q g_j(x)\|)_j\|_{\ell_q} \, dx \leq 2 \int G .
\]
If moreover $n \geq 1$, $\int G < \infty$ and $t > 0$, then the good parts for the maximal big
cubes of $G$ at height $t$ satisfy
\[
  \|(\|\mathcal G g_j(x)\|)_j\|_{\ell_q} \leq 2^n t \quad \text{for almost every } x \in V
\]
and
\[
  \int \|(\|\mathcal G g_j(x)\|)_j\|_{\ell_q}^2 \, dx \leq 2^n t \int G .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
By \Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-signed-good}, $\|\mathcal G g_j\| \leq \mathcal G \|g_j\|$ for
every $j$, so the first and the fourth bound are those of
\Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-good-parts} for the family $(\|g_j\|)_j$, and the fifth follows by
\Cref{lem:norm-mean-square-bound}. For the bad pieces,
$\int \|(\|b_Q g_j\|)_j\|_{\ell_q} = \int_Q \|(\|g_j - (g_j)_Q\|)_j\|_{\ell_q} \leq 2 \int_Q G$
by \Cref{lem:norm-mean-square-bound}, since $|Q| < \infty$ (\Cref{lem:dyadic-cubes}), and
\Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-averages} sums these bounds over the maximal big cubes.
\end{proof}

\section{The weak type \texorpdfstring{$(1,1)$}{(1,1)} of vector-valued singular integrals}
\label{sec:vector-valued-weak-type}

Let $(\theta_j)_{j \in \N}$ be a Calder\'on--Zygmund family on $V$ with overlap $B$ and
H\"ormander constant $H$ (\Cref{def:cz-family}). This section proves the weak type $(1,1)$ of
the analysis operator $f \mapsto (\theta_j * f)_j$ and of the synthesis operators
$(g_j)_j \mapsto \sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j$ for finite sets $s \subseteq \N$. At a height
$t$, the signed Calder\'on--Zygmund decomposition of \Cref{sec:calderon-zygmund-signed} splits
$f$ into the good part $\mathcal G f$, which the Plancherel bounds of
\Cref{cor:cz-family-l2-bounds} control in $L_2$, and the bad part $\mathcal B f$, a sum of
pieces $b_Q f$ with mean zero. A maximal big cube $Q = Q_{k,m}$ has centre $c_Q$ and lies in the
closed ball $\bar B(c_Q, \rho_Q)$ with $\rho_Q = n 2^{-k}$ (\Cref{lem:dyadic-cubes}), and the
enlarged exceptional set $\Omega^*$ is the union of the balls $\bar B(c_Q, 2 \rho_Q)$
(\Cref{def:calderon-zygmund-cubes}). Off $\Omega^*$ the mean zero of the pieces lets the
H\"ormander condition act. This is the classical argument for singular integrals with values in a
Hilbert space~\cite{BenedekCalderonPanzone}; see also Stein~\cite{SteinSingular} and
Grafakos~\cite{Grafakos}.

\begin{lemma}[Elementary facts]
\label{lem:weak-type-elementary}
\lean{ENNReal.half_lt_or_half_lt_of_lt_add,
  MeasureTheory.memLp_two_of_lintegral_enorm_sq_ne_top}
\leanok
For all $t, a, b \in [0, \infty]$ with $t < a + b$, $t/2 < a$ or $t/2 < b$. For every measure
space $(X, \mu)$, every normed group $E$ and every almost everywhere strongly measurable
$f : X \to E$ with $\int \|f\|^2 \, d\mu < \infty$, $f \in L_2(\mu)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
If $a \leq t/2$ and $b \leq t/2$, then $a + b \leq t$ (Mathlib's
\texttt{lt\_\allowbreak or\_\allowbreak lt\_\allowbreak of\_\allowbreak add\_\allowbreak
lt\_\allowbreak add}). The second statement is the definition of the $L_2$ norm.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Level sets of a split function]
\label{lem:level-sets-split-function}
\lean{MeasureTheory.measure_half_lt_le_lintegral_sq,
  MeasureTheory.measure_half_lt_le_add_setLIntegral_compl,
  MeasureTheory.measure_lt_le_of_ae_le_add}
\leanok
\uses{lem:weak-type-elementary}
For every measure space $(X, \mu)$, every $t \in (0, \infty)$, all almost everywhere measurable
$a, b : X \to [0, \infty]$ and every measurable set $S \subseteq X$,
\[
  \mu\{a > t/2\} \leq 4 t^{-2} \int a^2 \, d\mu , \qquad
  \mu\{b > t/2\} \leq \mu(S) + 2 t^{-1} \int_{X \setminus S} b \, d\mu .
\]
For every $u : X \to [0, \infty]$ with $u \leq a + b$ almost everywhere and all
$A, D, K, I \in [0, \infty]$ with
\[
  \int a^2 \, d\mu \leq A t I , \qquad \mu(S) \leq D t^{-1} I , \qquad
  \int_{X \setminus S} b \, d\mu \leq K I ,
\]
$\mu\{u > t\} \leq (4A + D + 2K) \, t^{-1} I$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The first bound is Chebyshev's inequality for $a^2$ at height $t^2/4$, the second Chebyshev's
inequality for $\mathbf 1_{X \setminus S} \, b$ at height $t/2$. By
\Cref{lem:weak-type-elementary}, almost every point of $\{u > t\}$ lies in
$\{a > t/2\} \cup \{b > t/2\}$, and the two bounds give
$\mu\{u > t\} \leq 4 t^{-2} A t I + D t^{-1} I + 2 t^{-1} K I$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The H\"ormander condition around a cube]
\label{lem:hormander-around-cube}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.setLIntegral_compl_closedBall_le, Rd.IsCZFamily.measurable_lqNorm_sub,
  Rd.IsCZFamily.setLIntegral_compl_closedBall_setLIntegral_le}
\leanok
\uses{def:cz-family, def:lq-norm}
For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$, every Calder\'on--Zygmund family $(\theta_j)_j$ on $V$ with
overlap $B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$, every $c \in V$, every $\rho \in \R$ and every
$y \in V$ with $\|y - c\| \leq \rho$,
\[
  \int_{\{\|x - c\| > 2\rho\}} \|(\theta_j(x - y) - \theta_j(x - c))_j\|_{\ell_2} \, dx \leq H .
\]
The function $(x, y) \mapsto \|(\theta_j(x - y) - \theta_j(x - c))_j\|_{\ell_2}$ is measurable
on $V \times V$, and for every measurable $Q \subseteq \bar B(c, \rho)$ and every almost
everywhere measurable $m : V \to [0, \infty]$,
\[
  \int_{\{\|x - c\| > 2\rho\}} \int_Q \|(\theta_j(x - y) - \theta_j(x - c))_j\|_{\ell_2} \,
  m(y) \, dy \, dx \leq H \int_Q m .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
Every $x$ with $\|x - c\| > 2\rho$ satisfies $\|x - c\| > 2 \|y - c\|$. The substitution
$x' = x - c$ turns the integral into one over a subset of $\{\|x'\| > 2 \|y - c\|\}$ with
integrand $\|(\theta_j(x' - (y - c)) - \theta_j(x'))_j\|_{\ell_2}$, which is at most $H$ by the
H\"ormander condition at $y - c$ (\Cref{def:cz-family}). The kernels are continuous, so the
function on $V \times V$ is measurable. Tonelli's theorem exchanges the two integrals in the
last bound, and the inner integral is at most $H$ for every $y \in Q$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Convolutions of pieces with mean zero]
\label{lem:mean-zero-pieces-conv}
\lean{Rd.enorm_conv_le_setLIntegral_sub, Rd.IsCZFamily.lqNorm_conv_le_setLIntegral,
  Rd.IsCZFamily.enorm_sum_conv_le_setLIntegral}
\leanok
\uses{def:cz-family, lem:reflect-basic, lem:minkowski-integral-lq,
  lem:lq-cauchy-schwarz-sequences}
For every continuous bounded $K : V \to \C$, every set $Q \subseteq V$, every integrable
$b : V \to \C$ with $b = 0$ outside $Q$ and $\int b = 0$, and all $c, x \in V$,
\[
  |(K * b)(x)| \leq \int_Q |K(x - y) - K(x - c)| \, |b(y)| \, dy .
\]
For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$, every Calder\'on--Zygmund family $(\theta_j)_j$ with overlap
$B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$, every such $b$ and all $c, x \in V$,
\[
  \|((\theta_j * b)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}
  \leq \int_Q \|(\theta_j(x - y) - \theta_j(x - c))_j\|_{\ell_2} \, |b(y)| \, dy ,
\]
and for every finite set $s \subseteq \N$ and all integrable $b_j : V \to \C$ with $b_j = 0$
outside $Q$ and $\int b_j = 0$,
\[
  \Bigl|\sum_{j \in s} (\theta_j * b_j)(x)\Bigr|
  \leq \int_Q \|(\theta_j(x - y) - \theta_j(x - c))_j\|_{\ell_2} \,
  \|(b_j(y))_j\|_{\ell_2} \, dy .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
By \Cref{lem:reflect-basic}, $(K * b)(x) = \int K(x - y) b(y) \, dy$, and since $\int b = 0$
this is $\int (K(x - y) - K(x - c)) b(y) \, dy$; the integrand vanishes outside $Q$. The second
bound follows by Minkowski's integral inequality in $\ell_2$
(\Cref{lem:minkowski-integral-lq}). For the third, the triangle inequality and the first bound
for each $j \in s$ give
$\int_Q \sum_{j \in s} |\theta_j(x - y) - \theta_j(x - c)| \, |b_j(y)| \, dy$, and the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality of \Cref{lem:lq-cauchy-schwarz-sequences} applies at each $y$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Convolution of the bad part]
\label{lem:conv-bad-part}
\lean{Rd.hasSum_conv_czBadPart}
\leanok
\uses{def:calderon-zygmund-signed, lem:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces,
  thm:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces-mean-mass, lem:reflect-basic}
For every $G : V \to [0, \infty]$ and every $t \in [0, \infty]$, with $Q$ running over the
maximal big cubes of $G$ at height $t$: for every continuous bounded $K : V \to \C$, every
integrable $f : V \to \C$ and every $x \in V$,
\[
  (K * \mathcal B f)(x) = \sum_Q (K * b_Q f)(x) ,
\]
and the series converges absolutely.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
With $|K| \leq M$,
$\sum_Q \int |K(x - y)| \, |b_Q f(y)| \, dy \leq M \sum_Q \int |b_Q f| \leq 2 M \int |f|$
by \Cref{thm:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces-mean-mass}, so the series of the integrals
$\int K(x - y) \, b_Q f(y) \, dy$ converges absolutely to the integral of the series, which is
$\int K(x - y) \, \mathcal B f(y) \, dy$ by \Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces}. Both sides
are convolutions by \Cref{lem:reflect-basic}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The bad part off the enlarged exceptional set]
\label{lem:bad-part-off-enlarged}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.setLIntegral_compl_czEnlarged_tsum_le,
  Rd.IsCZFamily.setLIntegral_lqNorm_conv_czBadC_le,
  Rd.IsCZFamily.setLIntegral_enorm_sum_conv_czBadC_le}
\leanok
\uses{lem:hormander-around-cube, lem:mean-zero-pieces-conv, lem:conv-bad-part,
  lem:lp-series-minkowski, thm:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces-mean-mass,
  thm:calderon-zygmund-signed-family, lem:dyadic-cubes, def:calderon-zygmund-cubes}
For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$, every Calder\'on--Zygmund family $(\theta_j)_j$ with overlap
$B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$, every $G : V \to [0, \infty]$ and every $t \in [0, \infty]$,
with the enlarged exceptional set $\Omega^*$ of the maximal big cubes $Q$ of $G$ at height $t$:
for every family of almost everywhere measurable $m_Q : V \to [0, \infty]$,
\[
  \int_{V \setminus \Omega^*} \sum_Q \int_Q
  \|(\theta_j(x - y) - \theta_j(x - c_Q))_j\|_{\ell_2} \, m_Q(y) \, dy \, dx
  \leq H \sum_Q \int_Q m_Q ;
\]
for every integrable $f : V \to \C$,
\[
  \int_{V \setminus \Omega^*} \|((\theta_j * \mathcal B f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \, dx
  \leq 2 H \int |f| ;
\]
and for every finite set $s \subseteq \N$ and all integrable $g_j : V \to \C$,
\[
  \int_{V \setminus \Omega^*} \Bigl|\sum_{j \in s} (\theta_j * \mathcal B g_j)(x)\Bigr| \, dx
  \leq 2 H \int \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \, dx .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
A point $x \notin \Omega^*$ satisfies $\|x - c_Q\| > 2\rho_Q$ for every maximal big cube $Q$,
and $Q \subseteq \bar B(c_Q, \rho_Q)$ (\Cref{lem:dyadic-cubes}). Monotone convergence and
\Cref{lem:hormander-around-cube} for each $Q$ give the first bound. By \Cref{lem:conv-bad-part},
Minkowski's inequality for series (\Cref{lem:lp-series-minkowski}) and
\Cref{lem:mean-zero-pieces-conv},
\[
  \|((\theta_j * \mathcal B f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}
  \leq \sum_Q \int_Q \|(\theta_j(x - y) - \theta_j(x - c_Q))_j\|_{\ell_2} \,
  |b_Q f(y)| \, dy
\]
for every $x$, so the first bound with $m_Q = |b_Q f|$ and
\Cref{thm:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces-mean-mass} give the second. The third follows in the same
way with $m_Q(y) = \|(b_Q g_j(y))_j\|_{\ell_2}$ and \Cref{thm:calderon-zygmund-signed-family}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The good part and the splitting]
\label{lem:good-part-split}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.ae_lqNorm_conv_le_add, Rd.IsCZFamily.ae_enorm_sum_conv_le_add,
  Rd.IsCZFamily.lintegral_lqNorm_conv_czGoodC_sq_le,
  Rd.IsCZFamily.lintegral_enorm_sum_conv_czGoodC_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{cor:cz-family-l2-bounds, thm:calderon-zygmund-signed-good-bounds,
  thm:calderon-zygmund-signed-family, lem:calderon-zygmund-signed-good,
  lem:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces, lem:conv-assoc, lem:weak-type-elementary, lem:lq-basic}
For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$, every Calder\'on--Zygmund family $(\theta_j)_j$ with overlap
$B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$, every $G : V \to [0, \infty]$ and every $t \in [0, \infty]$:
for every integrable $f : V \to \C$ and almost every $x \in V$,
\[
  \|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \leq \|((\theta_j * \mathcal G f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}
  + \|((\theta_j * \mathcal B f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} ,
\]
and for every finite set $s \subseteq \N$, all integrable $g_j : V \to \C$ and almost every
$x \in V$,
\[
  \Bigl|\sum_{j \in s} (\theta_j * g_j)(x)\Bigr|
  \leq \Bigl|\sum_{j \in s} (\theta_j * \mathcal G g_j)(x)\Bigr|
  + \Bigl|\sum_{j \in s} (\theta_j * \mathcal B g_j)(x)\Bigr| .
\]
If moreover $n \geq 1$ and $0 < t < \infty$, then for every integrable $f : V \to \C$ and the
cubes of $|f|$ at height $t$,
\[
  \int \|((\theta_j * \mathcal G f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}^2 \, dx \leq B \, 2^n t \int |f| ,
\]
and for every finite set $s \subseteq \N$, all almost everywhere strongly measurable
$g_j : V \to \C$ with $\int \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \, dx < \infty$ and the cubes of
$x \mapsto \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}$ at height $t$,
\[
  \int \Bigl|\sum_{j \in s} (\theta_j * \mathcal G g_j)(x)\Bigr|^2 \, dx
  \leq B \, 2^n t \int \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \, dx .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
By \Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces}, $f = \mathcal G f + \mathcal B f$, and both parts
are integrable
(\Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-signed-good}, \Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-bad-pieces}); convolution
is additive almost everywhere (\Cref{lem:conv-assoc}), and Minkowski's inequality in $\ell_2$
(\Cref{lem:lq-basic}) gives the first bound, the triangle inequality the second. For the good
parts, $\int |\mathcal G f|^2 \leq 2^n t \int |f| < \infty$
(\Cref{thm:calderon-zygmund-signed-good-bounds}), and
$|\mathcal G g_j| \leq \|(\mathcal G g_i)_i\|_{\ell_2}$, whose square has integral at most
$2^n t \int \|(g_i)_i\|_{\ell_2}$ (\Cref{thm:calderon-zygmund-signed-family}). So the good parts
lie in $L_2$ (\Cref{lem:weak-type-elementary}), and \Cref{cor:cz-family-l2-bounds} gives the
last two bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The weak type constant]
\label{def:vector-weak-const}
\lean{Rd.vectorWeakConst, Rd.vectorWeakConst_ne_top}
\leanok
For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$,
\[
  C_V(B, H) = 4 \cdot 2^n B + (2n)^n \, |B(0, 1)| + 4 H ,
\]
where $|B(0, 1)|$ is the volume of the unit ball of $V$. It is finite if $B$ and $H$ are.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The weak type $(1,1)$ of vector-valued singular integrals]
\label{thm:vector-valued-weak-type}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.volume_lqNorm_conv_gt_le, Rd.IsCZFamily.volume_enorm_sum_conv_gt_le}
\leanok
\uses{lem:level-sets-split-function, lem:good-part-split, lem:bad-part-off-enlarged,
  lem:calderon-zygmund-averages, def:vector-weak-const}
Let $n \geq 1$. For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$, every Calder\'on--Zygmund family
$(\theta_j)_j$ on $V$ with overlap $B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$ and every
$t \in (0, \infty)$:
for every integrable $f : V \to \C$,
\[
  \bigl|\{x \in V : \|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} > t\}\bigr|
  \leq C_V(B, H) \, t^{-1} \int |f| ,
\]
and for every finite set $s \subseteq \N$ and all almost everywhere strongly measurable
$g_j : V \to \C$ with $\int \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \, dx < \infty$,
\[
  \Bigl|\Bigl\{x \in V : \Bigl|\sum_{j \in s} (\theta_j * g_j)(x)\Bigr| > t\Bigr\}\Bigr|
  \leq C_V(B, H) \, t^{-1} \int \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \, dx .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
Decompose $f$ along the maximal big cubes of $|f|$ at height $t$, and every $g_j$ along those
of $\|(g_j)_j\|_{\ell_2}$; the $g_j$ are integrable, since $|g_j| \leq \|(g_i)_i\|_{\ell_2}$.
Apply \Cref{lem:level-sets-split-function} with the sizes of the good and of the bad parts as $a$
and $b$ and with $S = \Omega^*$: \Cref{lem:good-part-split} gives the splitting and $A = B 2^n$,
\Cref{lem:calderon-zygmund-averages} gives $D = (2n)^n |B(0, 1)|$, and
\Cref{lem:bad-part-off-enlarged} gives $K = 2H$. Then $4A + D + 2K = C_V(B, H)$.
\end{proof}

\section{Weak \texorpdfstring{$L_p$}{L\_p} norms and operators of weak and strong type}
\label{sec:weak-type-operators}

The definitions of this section are those of the formalisation of Carleson's theorem
\cite{CarlesonLean} (\url{https://github.com/fpvandoorn/carleson}), taken over with the same
names and statements; that project intends them for Mathlib. Functions take values in a type
$E$ with an extended norm $\|\cdot\| : E \to [0, \infty]$, such as $\C$ or $[0, \infty]$
itself, and operators $T$ map functions on a measure space $(X, \mu)$ to functions on a measure
space $(Y, \nu)$.

\begin{definition}[Weak $L_p$ norms and weak type {\cite{CarlesonLean}}]
\label{def:weak-type-operators}
\lean{MeasureTheory.distribution, MeasureTheory.wnorm', MeasureTheory.wnorm,
  MeasureTheory.MemWLp, MeasureTheory.HasWeakType, MeasureTheory.HasStrongType,
  MeasureTheory.AESubadditiveOn}
\leanok
For every $f : X \to E$ and every $t \in [0, \infty]$, the distribution function of $f$ is
$d_f(t) = \mu\{x \in X : \|f(x)\| > t\}$. For every real $q \neq 0$,
\[
  w_q(f) = \sup_{t \geq 0} t \, d_f(t)^{1/q} ;
\]
for $p \in (0, \infty)$ the weak $L_p$ norm is $\|f\|_{p, \infty} = w_p(f)$,
$\|f\|_{\infty, \infty}$ is the essential supremum of $\|f\|$, and $\|f\|_{0, \infty} = \infty$;
the function $f$ lies in weak $L_p(\mu)$ if it is almost everywhere strongly measurable and
$\|f\|_{p, \infty} < \infty$. For all $p, q, C \in [0, \infty]$, an operator $T$ has weak type
$(p, q)$ with constant $C$ if for every $f \in L_p(\mu)$ the function $T f$ is almost everywhere
strongly measurable and $\|T f\|_{q, \infty} \leq C \|f\|_p$, and strong type $(p, q)$ with
constant $C$ if for every $f \in L_p(\mu)$ the function $T f$ is almost everywhere strongly
measurable and $\|T f\|_q \leq C \|f\|_p$. For every property $P$ of functions on $X$ and every
$A \in [0, \infty]$, $T$ is almost everywhere subadditive on $P$ with constant $A$ if for all
$f, g$ with property $P$,
$\|T(f + g)(y)\| \leq A (\|T f(y)\| + \|T g(y)\|)$ for $\nu$-almost every $y \in Y$.
\end{definition}

The value $\|f\|_{0, \infty} = \infty$ comes from Lean's convention $1/0 = 0$, under which
$\|f\|_{0, \infty} = \sup_{t \geq 0} t \, d_f(t)^0 = \sup_{t \geq 0} t$.

\begin{lemma}[Elementary properties]
\label{lem:distribution-weak-norm-basic}
\lean{MeasureTheory.distribution_top, MeasureTheory.distribution_mono_left,
  MeasureTheory.distribution_mono_right, MeasureTheory.distribution_add_le_of_enorm,
  MeasureTheory.wnorm_ne_top, MeasureTheory.mul_distribution_le_wnorm_one,
  MeasureTheory.distribution_le_inv_rpow_mul_eLpNorm_rpow, MeasureTheory.wnorm'_le_eLpNorm',
  MeasureTheory.wnorm_le_eLpNorm, MeasureTheory.MemLp.memWLp, MeasureTheory.HasWeakType.memWLp,
  MeasureTheory.HasStrongType.memLp, MeasureTheory.HasStrongType.hasWeakType}
\leanok
\uses{def:weak-type-operators}
For all $f : X \to E$ and $s, t \in [0, \infty]$: $d_f(\infty) = 0$; if $s \leq t$, then
$d_f(t) \leq d_f(s)$; for every type $E'$ with an extended norm and every $g : X \to E'$ with
$\|f\| \leq \|g\|$ almost everywhere, $d_f(t) \leq d_g(t)$; for all types $E_1, E_2$ with
extended norms, all $g_1 : X \to E_1$, $g_2 : X \to E_2$ and every $c \in [0, \infty]$ with
$\|f\| \leq c (\|g_1\| + \|g_2\|)$ almost everywhere,
\[
  d_f(c (t + s)) \leq d_{g_1}(t) + d_{g_2}(s) ;
\]
and $t \, d_f(t) \leq \|f\|_{1, \infty}$. For every $p \in (0, \infty)$,
$\|f\|_{p, \infty} = w_p(f)$, and for $t > 0$,
\[
  d_f(t) \leq t^{-p} \|f\|_p^p .
\]
For every almost everywhere strongly measurable $f$ and every $p \in (0, \infty]$,
$\|f\|_{p, \infty} \leq \|f\|_p$, so $L_p(\mu)$ lies in weak $L_p(\mu)$. For all
$p, q, C \in [0, \infty]$ with $C < \infty$, an operator of weak type $(p, q)$ with constant $C$
maps $L_p(\mu)$ into weak $L_q(\nu)$, and one of strong type $(p, q)$ maps $L_p(\mu)$ into
$L_q(\nu)$; for $q > 0$, strong type $(p, q)$ with constant $C$ implies weak type $(p, q)$ with
constant $C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The first four statements compare the sets $\{\|f\| > t\}$: no extended norm exceeds $\infty$,
the sets shrink as $t$ grows, they grow with $\|f\|$, and $\|g_1\| \leq t$, $\|g_2\| \leq s$
force $\|f\| \leq c (t + s)$. The bound by $\|f\|_{1, \infty}$ is one term of the supremum, and
$d_f(t) \leq t^{-p} \|f\|_p^p$ is Chebyshev's inequality (Mathlib's
\texttt{meas\_\allowbreak ge\_\allowbreak le\_\allowbreak mul\_\allowbreak pow\_\allowbreak
eLpNorm\_\allowbreak enorm}). It gives $t \, d_f(t)^{1/p} \leq \|f\|_p$ for every $t$, hence
$\|f\|_{p, \infty} \leq \|f\|_p$; for $p = \infty$ both sides are the essential supremum. The
statements on operators follow.
\end{proof}

\section{Marcinkiewicz interpolation}
\label{sec:marcinkiewicz}

For $1 < p < 2$, an operator that is almost everywhere subadditive with constant $A$, of weak
type $(1,1)$ with constant $C_1$ and of strong type $(2,2)$ with constant $C_2$ has strong type
$(p, p)$. Since strong type $(2,2)$ implies weak type $(2,2)$
(\Cref{lem:distribution-weak-norm-basic}), the real interpolation theorem of the formalisation
of Carleson's theorem \cite{CarlesonLean} with $(p_0, q_0) = (1, 1)$ and
$(p_1, q_1) = (2, 2)$ gives strong type $(p, p)$ for $A \geq 1$ and positive finite constants.
Here the layer cake argument gives it on s-finite measure spaces for every $A \geq 0$ and all
$C_1, C_2 \in [0, \infty]$, with the constant
$\bigl(p (2 A C_1/(p - 1) + 4 A^2 C_2^2/(2 - p))\bigr)^{1/p}$. The proof is the argument of
\Cref{thm:fefferman-stein-interpolation} on a general measure space: at each level $\tau$ the
input is split along the set where its size exceeds $\tau$, the weak type controls the large
part and the $L_2$ bound the small part, and the layer cake formula of \Cref{lem:layer-cake}
collects the levels. The measure $\mu$ on the input space is s-finite, so that Tonelli's theorem
applies; $\nu$ is any measure. The theorem is Marcinkiewicz's~\cite{Marcinkiewicz1939}, and
this proof is classical; see Stein~\cite{SteinSingular} and Grafakos~\cite{Grafakos}.

\begin{lemma}[{Layer cake formula for functions with values in $[0, \infty]$}]
\label{lem:layer-cake}
\lean{ENNReal.lt_toReal_min_natCast_iff, MeasureTheory.lintegral_min_natCast_rpow_eq,
  ENNReal.iSup_min_natCast_rpow, MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_eq_lintegral_meas_lt_mul_ennreal}
\leanok
For every measure space $(X, \nu)$, every almost everywhere measurable
$F : X \to [0, \infty]$ and every $p > 0$,
\[
  \int F^p \, d\nu = p \int_0^\infty \nu(\{F > t\}) \, t^{p-1} \, dt .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
For the truncation $\min(F, N)$, $N \in \N$, this is Mathlib's layer cake formula for real
functions (\texttt{lintegral\_rpow\_eq\_lintegral\_meas\_lt\_mul}), and for $t > 0$,
$\min(F, N) > t$ holds exactly when $F > t$ and $N > t$, so the right side is the integral
over $(0, N)$. As $N \to \infty$ the left side converges by monotone convergence and the right
side by the increasing union $\bigcup_N (0, N) = (0, \infty)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Integrals of powers]
\label{lem:power-integrals}
\lean{MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioo_rpow, MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_rpow_eq_top,
  MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_rpow_indicator_lt, MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_rpow_indicator_ge}
\leanok
For every $r > -1$ and every $a \in [0, \infty]$,
\[
  \int_{(0, \infty)} \mathbf 1_{\{t < a\}} \, t^r \, dt = \frac{a^{r+1}}{r + 1} .
\]
For every $r < -1$ and every $a \in [0, \infty]$,
\[
  \int_{(0, \infty)} \mathbf 1_{\{t \geq a\}} \, t^r \, dt = \frac{a^{r+1}}{-(r + 1)} .
\]
Here $\infty^{r+1} = \infty$ and $0^{r+1} = 0$ for $r + 1 > 0$, and $\infty^{r+1} = 0$ and
$0^{r+1} = \infty$ for $r + 1 < 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
For $0 < a < \infty$ these are the integrals of $t^r$ over $(0, a)$ and $[a, \infty)$ (Mathlib's
\texttt{integral\_rpow} and \texttt{integral\_Ioi\_rpow\_of\_lt}), and the first formula also
holds for $a = 0$. The integral of $t^r$ over $(0, \infty)$ is infinite for every $r$, since
$t^r$ is not integrable on $(0, \infty)$ (Mathlib's \texttt{not\_integrableOn\_Ioi\_rpow}); this
is the first integral for $a = \infty$ and the second for $a = 0$. For $a = \infty$ the second
integral vanishes.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The parts above and below a level]
\label{lem:parts-above-below-level}
\lean{MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_lt_le, MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_compl_rpow_le,
  MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_lt_ne_top,
  MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_compl_rpow_ne_top}
\leanok
For every measure space $(X, \mu)$, every $F : X \to [0, \infty]$, every $p \geq 1$ and every
$s \in (0, \infty)$,
\[
  \int_{\{F > s\}} F \, d\mu \leq s^{1-p} \int F^p \, d\mu ,
\]
and for all real $p, r$ with $0 \leq p \leq r$ and $0 < r$ and every $s \in [0, \infty)$,
\[
  \int_{\{F \leq s\}} F^r \, d\mu \leq s^{r-p} \int F^p \, d\mu .
\]
In particular both left sides are finite if $\int F^p \, d\mu < \infty$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
On $\{F > s\}$, $s^{p-1} F \leq F^p$; on $\{F \leq s\}$, $F^r = F^p F^{r-p} \leq F^p s^{r-p}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Two Tonelli steps]
\label{lem:tonelli-steps-measure-space}
\lean{MeasureTheory.measurable_indicator_section, MeasureTheory.measurableSet_ofReal_lt,
  ENNReal.rpow_mul_rpow_sub_le, MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_lintegral_indicator_lt_mul_rpow,
  MeasureTheory.lintegral_Ioi_lintegral_indicator_compl_mul_rpow_le}
\leanok
\uses{lem:power-integrals}
For every s-finite measure space $(X, \mu)$, every measurable $F : X \to [0, \infty]$ and every
$p > 1$,
\[
  \int_0^\infty \tau^{p-2} \int_{\{F > \tau\}} F \, d\mu \, d\tau
  = \frac{1}{p - 1} \int F^p \, d\mu ,
\]
and for every $r > 0$ and every $p < r$,
\[
  \int_0^\infty \tau^{p-1-r} \int_{\{F \leq \tau\}} F^r \, d\mu \, d\tau
  \leq \frac{1}{r - p} \int F^p \, d\mu .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The integrands are jointly measurable in $(\tau, x)$, so Tonelli's theorem for the s-finite
measure $\mu$ and Lebesgue measure on $(0, \infty)$ exchanges the integrals. By
\Cref{lem:power-integrals}, $\int_0^{F(x)} \tau^{p-2} \, d\tau = F(x)^{p-1}/(p-1)$ and
$\int_{F(x)}^\infty \tau^{p-1-r} \, d\tau = F(x)^{p-r}/(r-p)$, and $F^r F^{p-r} \leq F^p$ in
$[0, \infty]$, with equality where $0 < F < \infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Integrals of powers from bounds at every level]
\label{lem:power-integral-from-levels}
\lean{MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_measure_lt_mul_rpow_le}
\leanok
\uses{lem:layer-cake, lem:tonelli-steps-measure-space}
For every s-finite measure space $(X, \mu)$, every measure space $(Y, \nu)$, every almost
everywhere measurable $F : Y \to [0, \infty]$, every measurable $G : X \to [0, \infty]$, all
real $p, r$ with $1 < p < r$ and all $K_1, K_2 \in [0, \infty]$: if for every $\tau > 0$
\[
  \nu\{F > \tau\} \, \tau^{p-1}
  \leq K_1 \, \tau^{p-2} \int_{\{G > \tau\}} G \, d\mu
  + K_2 \, \tau^{p-1-r} \int_{\{G \leq \tau\}} G^r \, d\mu ,
\]
then
\[
  \int F^p \, d\nu \leq p \Bigl( \frac{K_1}{p - 1} + \frac{K_2}{r - p} \Bigr) \int G^p \, d\mu .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
By \Cref{lem:layer-cake}, $\int F^p \, d\nu = p \int_0^\infty \nu\{F > \tau\} \tau^{p-1} \,
d\tau$. Bound the integrand by the hypothesis and evaluate the two integrals over $\tau$ by
\Cref{lem:tonelli-steps-measure-space}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The level estimate]
\label{lem:marcinkiewicz-level}
\lean{ENNReal.inv_half_mul_ofReal_rpow, ENNReal.inv_half_rpow_mul_ofReal_rpow,
  MeasureTheory.measure_lt_mul_rpow_le_of_le_add}
\leanok
\uses{lem:distribution-weak-norm-basic}
For every $\tau > 0$ and all real $p, r$,
\[
  (\tau/2)^{-1} \tau^{p-1} = 2 \tau^{p-2} , \qquad
  (\tau/2)^{-r} \tau^{p-1} = 2^r \tau^{p-1-r} .
\]
For every measure space $(Y, \nu)$, all $F, F_1, F_2 : Y \to [0, \infty]$ with $F_2$ almost
everywhere measurable and $F \leq F_1 + F_2$ almost everywhere, every $\tau > 0$, every real
$p$ and all $C_1, C_2, I_1, I_2 \in [0, \infty]$ with
\[
  \nu\{F_1 > \tau/2\} \leq C_1 (\tau/2)^{-1} I_1 , \qquad \int F_2^2 \, d\nu \leq C_2 I_2 ,
\]
the bound
$\nu\{F > \tau\} \, \tau^{p-1} \leq 2 C_1 \tau^{p-2} I_1 + 4 C_2 \tau^{p-3} I_2$ holds.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The identities are computations with real powers. Almost every point of $\{F > \tau\}$ lies in
$\{F_1 > \tau/2\} \cup \{F_2 > \tau/2\}$ (the distribution of a sum in
\Cref{lem:distribution-weak-norm-basic}, with $c = 1$), and Chebyshev's inequality gives
$\nu\{F_2 > \tau/2\} \leq (\tau/2)^{-2} C_2 I_2$. The identities with $r = 2$ finish the proof.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The Marcinkiewicz constants]
\label{def:marcinkiewicz-const}
\lean{MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczConst, MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczConst_ne_top,
  MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczNormConst, MeasureTheory.marcinkiewiczNormConst_ne_top}
\leanok
For $1 < p < 2$ and all $A, C_1, C_2 \in [0, \infty]$,
\[
  C^{\mathrm M}_p(C_1, C_2) = p \Bigl( \frac{2 C_1}{p - 1} + \frac{4 C_2}{2 - p} \Bigr)
\]
and $N_p(A, C_1, C_2) = C^{\mathrm M}_p(A C_1, A^2 C_2^2)^{1/p}$. Both are finite for finite
$A$, $C_1$, $C_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The layer cake argument of Marcinkiewicz interpolation]
\label{thm:marcinkiewicz-layer-cake}
\lean{MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_forall_le_add}
\leanok
\uses{lem:power-integral-from-levels, lem:marcinkiewicz-level, def:marcinkiewicz-const}
Let $(X, \mu)$ be an s-finite measure space, $(Y, \nu)$ a measure space and $1 < p < 2$. For
every almost everywhere measurable $F : Y \to [0, \infty]$, every measurable
$G : X \to [0, \infty]$, all $C_1, C_2 \in [0, \infty]$ and all families
$F_{1, \tau}, F_{2, \tau} : Y \to [0, \infty]$, $\tau > 0$, with $F_{2, \tau}$ almost everywhere
measurable, $F \leq F_{1, \tau} + F_{2, \tau}$ almost everywhere,
\[
  \nu\{F_{1, \tau} > \tau/2\} \leq C_1 (\tau/2)^{-1} \int_{\{G > \tau\}} G \, d\mu
\]
and
\[
  \int F_{2, \tau}^2 \, d\nu \leq C_2 \int_{\{G \leq \tau\}} G^2 \, d\mu
\]
for every $\tau > 0$,
\[
  \int F^p \, d\nu \leq C^{\mathrm M}_p(C_1, C_2) \int G^p \, d\mu .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
\Cref{lem:marcinkiewicz-level} gives the hypothesis of \Cref{lem:power-integral-from-levels}
with $r = 2$, $K_1 = 2 C_1$ and $K_2 = 4 C_2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[From integrals of powers to $L_p$ norms]
\label{lem:lp-norm-from-power-integrals}
\lean{MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_lintegral_enorm_le,
  MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_rpow_mul_of_lintegral_le,
  MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_sq_eq_eLpNorm_sq}
\leanok
\uses{lem:minkowski-avg, lem:lp-norm-nonnegative}
For all measure spaces $(X, \mu)$, $(Y, \nu)$, all types $E, E'$ with an extended norm, every
$p \in (0, \infty)$, every $C \in [0, \infty]$ and all almost everywhere strongly measurable
$F : Y \to E$, $G : X \to E'$ with $\int \|F\|^p \, d\nu \leq C \int \|G\|^p \, d\mu$,
\[
  \|F\|_{L_p(\nu)} \leq C^{1/p} \, \|G\|_{L_p(\mu)} .
\]
For every almost everywhere strongly measurable $g : X \to E$,
$\int \|g\|^2 \, d\mu = \|g\|_{L_2(\mu)}^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
Both follow from $\|F\|_p^p = \int \|F\|^p$ (the identity
\texttt{MeasureTheory.\allowbreak eLpNorm\_\allowbreak rpow\_\allowbreak eq}, cited in
\Cref{lem:minkowski-avg}; \Cref{lem:lp-norm-nonnegative} for $[0, \infty]$-valued functions),
the first by taking $p$-th roots.
\end{proof}

The first form of the interpolation theorem works with an abstract input type: every input
$x$ has a size $G_x : X \to [0, \infty]$, such as $|f|$ for a function $f$ or
$\|(g_j)_j\|_{\ell_2}$ for a family $(g_j)_j$, and can be restricted to measurable sets.

\begin{theorem}[Marcinkiewicz interpolation for operators on an abstract input type]
\label{thm:marcinkiewicz-abstract}
\lean{MeasureTheory.lintegral_rpow_le_of_weak_one_strong_two,
  MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_weak_one_strong_two}
\leanok
\uses{thm:marcinkiewicz-layer-cake, lem:parts-above-below-level,
  lem:lp-norm-from-power-integrals}
Let $(X, \mu)$ be an s-finite measure space, $(Y, \nu)$ a measure space, $\mathcal X$ a set,
$1 < p < 2$ and $C_1, C_2 \in [0, \infty]$. Let every $x \in \mathcal X$ carry a measurable
$G_x : X \to [0, \infty]$ and an almost everywhere measurable $T x : Y \to [0, \infty]$, and let
every measurable $S \subseteq X$ give an element $x|_S \in \mathcal X$ with
$G_{x|_S} = \mathbf 1_S G_x$. Suppose that for every $x \in \mathcal X$
\begin{itemize}
  \item if $\int G_x^p \, d\mu < \infty$, then $T x \leq T(x|_S) + T(x|_{X \setminus S})$
  $\nu$-almost everywhere for every measurable $S \subseteq X$;
  \item if $\int G_x \, d\mu < \infty$, then $\nu\{T x > t\} \leq C_1 t^{-1} \int G_x \, d\mu$
  for every $t \in (0, \infty)$;
  \item if $\int G_x^2 \, d\mu < \infty$, then
  $\int (T x)^2 \, d\nu \leq C_2 \int G_x^2 \, d\mu$.
\end{itemize}
Then for every $x \in \mathcal X$ with $\int G_x^p \, d\mu < \infty$,
\[
  \int (T x)^p \, d\nu \leq C^{\mathrm M}_p(C_1, C_2) \int G_x^p \, d\mu
\]
and
\[
  \|T x\|_{L_p(\nu)} \leq C^{\mathrm M}_p(C_1, C_2)^{1/p} \, \|G_x\|_{L_p(\mu)} .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
Apply \Cref{thm:marcinkiewicz-layer-cake} with $F = T x$, $G = G_x$,
$F_{1, \tau} = T(x|_{S_\tau})$ and $F_{2, \tau} = T(x|_{X \setminus S_\tau})$ for
$S_\tau = \{G_x > \tau\}$. The restricted inputs satisfy the finiteness conditions:
$\int_{S_\tau} G_x \leq \tau^{1-p} \int G_x^p$ and
$\int_{X \setminus S_\tau} G_x^2 \leq \tau^{2-p} \int G_x^p$ by
\Cref{lem:parts-above-below-level}. \Cref{lem:lp-norm-from-power-integrals} turns the first
bound into the second.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Truncation at a level]
\label{lem:truncation-level}
\lean{MeasureTheory.measure_lt_mul_enorm_le_wnorm_one,
  MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_enorm_sq_le_of_hasStrongType, MeasureTheory.ae_enorm_indicator_eq,
  MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_indicator_rpow_eq, MeasureTheory.memLp_one_indicator_lt,
  MeasureTheory.memLp_two_indicator_compl}
\leanok
\uses{def:weak-type-operators, lem:distribution-weak-norm-basic, lem:parts-above-below-level,
  lem:lp-norm-from-power-integrals}
For every measure space $(Y, \nu)$, every $g : Y \to E$, every $A \geq 0$ and every
$t \in (0, \infty)$, $\nu\{A \|g\| > t\} \leq A t^{-1} \|g\|_{1, \infty}$. For every operator
$T$ of strong type $(2, 2)$ with constant $C_2$, every $g \in L_2(\mu)$ and every $A \geq 0$,
$\int (A \|T g\|)^2 \, d\nu \leq A^2 C_2^2 \int \|g\|^2 \, d\mu$. Let $E$ be a monoid with an
extended seminorm, $f : X \to E$ almost everywhere strongly measurable and
$G : X \to [0, \infty]$ measurable with $\|f\| = G$ almost everywhere. Then for every
$S \subseteq X$, $\|\mathbf 1_S f\| = \mathbf 1_S G$ almost everywhere, and
$\int \|\mathbf 1_S f\|^r = \int (\mathbf 1_S G)^r$ for every real $r$. If
$\int G^p \, d\mu < \infty$, then $\mathbf 1_{\{G > \tau\}} f \in L_1(\mu)$ for $p \geq 1$ and
every $\tau > 0$, and $\mathbf 1_{\{G \leq \tau\}} f \in L_2(\mu)$ for $0 \leq p \leq 2$ and
every real $\tau$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
For $A > 0$, $\{A \|g\| > t\} = \{\|g\| > t/A\}$, and \Cref{lem:distribution-weak-norm-basic}
gives $(t/A) \, d_g(t/A) \leq \|g\|_{1, \infty}$; for $A = 0$ the set is empty. The second bound
is the square of $\|T g\|_2 \leq C_2 \|g\|_2$ (\Cref{lem:lp-norm-from-power-integrals}). The
norm of $\mathbf 1_S f$ is $\mathbf 1_S \|f\|$. Finally
$\int_{\{G > \tau\}} G \leq \tau^{1-p} \int G^p$ and
$\int_{\{G \leq \tau\}} G^2 \leq \tau^{2-p} \int G^p$ (\Cref{lem:parts-above-below-level}).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Marcinkiewicz interpolation between weak type $(1,1)$ and strong type $(2,2)$]
\label{thm:marcinkiewicz-interpolation}
\lean{MeasureTheory.lintegral_enorm_rpow_le_of_hasWeakType_of_hasStrongType,
  MeasureTheory.hasStrongType_of_hasWeakType_one_of_hasStrongType_two}
\leanok
\uses{thm:marcinkiewicz-layer-cake, lem:lp-norm-from-power-integrals, lem:truncation-level,
  def:weak-type-operators, def:marcinkiewicz-const}
Let $(X, \mu)$ be an s-finite measure space, $(Y, \nu)$ a measure space, $E$ a monoid with an
extended seminorm, $Z$ a type with an extended norm, $A \geq 0$ and
$C_1, C_2 \in [0, \infty]$. Let $T$ map functions $X \to E$ to functions $Y \to Z$, be almost
everywhere subadditive with constant $A$ on the functions in $L_1(\mu)$ or $L_2(\mu)$, of weak
type $(1, 1)$ with constant $C_1$ and of strong type $(2, 2)$ with constant $C_2$. Then for every
real $p$ with $1 < p < 2$ and every almost everywhere strongly measurable $f : X \to E$ with
$\int \|f\|^p \, d\mu < \infty$ and almost everywhere strongly measurable $T f$,
\[
  \int \|T f\|^p \, d\nu \leq C^{\mathrm M}_p(A C_1, A^2 C_2^2) \int \|f\|^p \, d\mu .
\]
If moreover $T f$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable for every $f \in L_p(\mu)$, then $T$
has strong type $(p, p)$ with constant $N_p(A, C_1, C_2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
Choose a measurable $G$ with $\|f\| = G$ almost everywhere, and for $\tau > 0$ split
$f = \mathbf 1_{\{G > \tau\}} f + \mathbf 1_{\{G \leq \tau\}} f$; the first part lies in
$L_1(\mu)$, the second in $L_2(\mu)$ (\Cref{lem:truncation-level}). Subadditivity gives
$\|T f\| \leq A \|T(\mathbf 1_{\{G > \tau\}} f)\| + A \|T(\mathbf 1_{\{G \leq \tau\}} f)\|$
almost everywhere. By \Cref{lem:truncation-level}, the weak type $(1,1)$ gives
\[
  \nu\{A \|T(\mathbf 1_{\{G > \tau\}} f)\| > \tau/2\}
  \leq A C_1 (\tau/2)^{-1} \int_{\{G > \tau\}} G ,
\]
and the strong type $(2,2)$ gives
$\int A^2 \|T(\mathbf 1_{\{G \leq \tau\}} f)\|^2 \leq A^2 C_2^2 \int_{\{G \leq \tau\}} G^2$.
\Cref{thm:marcinkiewicz-layer-cake} gives the first bound, and
\Cref{lem:lp-norm-from-power-integrals} the strong type.
\end{proof}

\section{\texorpdfstring{$L_p$}{L\_p} norms by duality}
\label{sec:lp-norm-duality}

For $1 < p < \infty$ with conjugate exponent $p' = p/(p - 1)$, a function in $L_p$ whose
pairings with all functions of $L_{p'}$ are bounded by $A$ times their $L_{p'}$ norm has $L_p$
norm at most $A$, and likewise for the mixed norm of $L_p(\ell_2)$ and families in $L_p$ that
vanish outside a finite set. The proof tests the pairing on one explicit family, the norming
family, and uses only H\"older's inequality. Throughout, $(X, \mu)$ is a measure space.

\begin{lemma}[H\"older's inequality in $L_p$ norms]
\label{lem:holder-lp-norms}
\lean{MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_le_eLpNorm_mul_eLpNorm}
\leanok
\uses{lem:lp-norm-nonnegative}
For all $p, q \in (1, \infty)$ with $1/p + 1/q = 1$ and all almost everywhere measurable
$F, G : X \to [0, \infty]$,
\[
  \int F G \, d\mu \leq \|F\|_{L_p(\mu)} \|G\|_{L_q(\mu)} .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
This is H\"older's inequality (Mathlib's
\texttt{ENNReal.\allowbreak lintegral\_\allowbreak mul\_\allowbreak le\_\allowbreak
Lp\_\allowbreak mul\_\allowbreak Lq}) written with $\|F\|_p^p = \int F^p$
(\Cref{lem:lp-norm-nonnegative}).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Families vanishing outside a finite set]
\label{lem:finite-families-lp-l2}
\lean{MeasureTheory.lqNorm_enorm_ne_top_of_finite, MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_ne_top_of_finite,
  MeasureTheory.lintegral_lqNorm_rpow_ne_top_of_finite,
  MeasureTheory.memLp_of_lintegral_lqNorm_rpow_ne_top}
\leanok
\uses{def:lq-norm, lem:lq-basic, lem:lp-series-minkowski, lem:lp-norm-nonnegative}
For every $p \geq 1$, every finite set $s \subseteq \N$ and all $u_j \in L_p(\mu)$, $j \in \N$,
with $u_j = 0$ for $j \notin s$, the pointwise norm $\|(u_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}$ is finite at every
$x \in X$ and $\bigl\| \|(u_j)_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_{L_p(\mu)} < \infty$; if moreover
$p < \infty$, then $\int \|(u_j)_j\|_{\ell_2}^p \, d\mu < \infty$. For every
$p \in (0, \infty)$, every family of functions $g_i : X \to \C$, $i \in \N$, and every $j \in \N$
with $g_j$ almost everywhere strongly measurable and
$\int \|(g_i)_i\|_{\ell_2}^p \, d\mu < \infty$, $g_j \in L_p(\mu)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
$\|(u_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \leq \sum_{j \in s} |u_j(x)|$ (\Cref{lem:lq-basic}), and Minkowski's
inequality (\Cref{lem:lp-series-minkowski}) bounds the $L_p$ norm of the right side by
$\sum_{j \in s} \|u_j\|_p$; the integral is the $p$-th power of this norm
(\Cref{lem:lp-norm-nonnegative}). The last statement holds since
$|g_j| \leq \|(g_i)_i\|_{\ell_2}$ (\Cref{lem:lq-basic}).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The norming family]
\label{def:norming-family}
\lean{MeasureTheory.normingFamily, MeasureTheory.aestronglyMeasurable_normingFamily}
\leanok
\uses{def:lq-norm}
For every real $p$ and every family $u = (u_j)_{j \in \N}$ of functions $X \to \C$, the
norming family of $u$ is
\[
  N_j(x) = u_j(x) \, \|(u_i(x))_i\|_{\ell_2}^{p-2} , \qquad j \in \N, \ x \in X,
\]
where the norm $\infty$ is replaced by $0$ before the real power is taken. If every $u_j$ is
almost everywhere strongly measurable, so is every $N_j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Size and pairing of the norming family]
\label{lem:norming-family}
\lean{MeasureTheory.lqNorm_normingFamily, MeasureTheory.sum_mul_conj_normingFamily,
  MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_normingFamily, MeasureTheory.memLp_normingFamily,
  MeasureTheory.enorm_sum_integral_mul_conj_normingFamily}
\leanok
\uses{def:norming-family, lem:lq-basic, lem:finite-families-lp-l2, lem:lp-norm-nonnegative}
For every real $p > 1$, every family $u$ of functions $X \to \C$ and every $x \in X$ with
$\|(u_i(x))_i\|_{\ell_2} < \infty$,
$\|(N_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} = \|(u_i(x))_i\|_{\ell_2}^{p-1}$. For every real $p > 0$, every finite
set $s \subseteq \N$ and every $x \in X$ with $u_j(x) = 0$ for $j \notin s$,
\[
  \sum_{j \in s} u_j(x) \, \overline{N_j(x)} = \|(u_i(x))_i\|_{\ell_2}^p .
\]
For all $1 < p < \infty$ and $q$ with $1/p + 1/q = 1$, every finite set $s \subseteq \N$ and all
$u_j \in L_p(\mu)$ with $u_j = 0$ for $j \notin s$, the integral
$I_u = \int \|(u_j)_j\|_{\ell_2}^p \, d\mu$ is finite, every $N_j$ lies in $L_q(\mu)$,
\[
  \bigl\| \|(N_j)_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_{L_q(\mu)} = I_u^{1/q} \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \Bigl| \sum_{j \in s} \int u_j \, \overline{N_j} \, d\mu \Bigr| = I_u .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
Every member of $u$ is multiplied by $r^{p-2}$ with $r = \|(u_i(x))_i\|_{\ell_2}$, so the
$\ell_2$ norm is $r^{p-2} r = r^{p-1}$ (\Cref{lem:lq-basic}). Since
$u_j \overline{u_j} = |u_j|^2$ and $\sum_{j \in s} |u_j(x)|^2 = r^2$, the sum is
$r^{p-2} r^2 = r^p$. For the last statement, $I_u < \infty$ by \Cref{lem:finite-families-lp-l2};
the first identity and $(p - 1) q = p$ give the norm of $(N_j)_j$, and $N_j \in L_q(\mu)$ since
$|N_j| \leq \|(N_i)_i\|_{\ell_2}$. The pairing is the integral of the second identity, a
nonnegative real function.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[$L_p$ norms by duality]
\label{thm:lp-norm-duality}
\lean{MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_lqNorm_le_of_forall_enorm_sum_integral_le,
  MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_of_forall_enorm_integral_mul_conj_le}
\leanok
\uses{lem:norming-family, lem:cancel-conjugate-power, lem:lp-norm-nonnegative, lem:lq-basic}
Let $1 < p < \infty$, $1/p + 1/q = 1$ and $A \in [0, \infty]$. For every finite set
$s \subseteq \N$ and all $u_j \in L_p(\mu)$, $j \in \N$, with $u_j = 0$ for $j \notin s$: if
\[
  \Bigl| \sum_{j \in s} \int u_j \, \overline{g_j} \, d\mu \Bigr|
  \leq A \, \bigl\| \|(g_j)_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_{L_q(\mu)}
\]
for every family of functions $g_j \in L_q(\mu)$, $j \in \N$, then
$\bigl\| \|(u_j)_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_{L_p(\mu)} \leq A$. For every $v \in L_p(\mu)$: if
$\bigl| \int v \, \overline g \, d\mu \bigr| \leq A \|g\|_{L_q(\mu)}$ for every
$g \in L_q(\mu)$, then $\|v\|_{L_p(\mu)} \leq A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
Test the hypothesis on the norming family $g = N$ for the exponent $p$
(\Cref{lem:norming-family}): $I_u \leq A I_u^{1/q}$ with $I_u < \infty$, so $I_u \leq A^p$ by
\Cref{lem:cancel-conjugate-power}, and
$\bigl\| \|(u_j)_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_p = I_u^{1/p} \leq A$. The second statement is the first
for the family $u_0 = v$, $u_j = 0$ for $j \geq 1$, since
$|g_0| \leq \|(g_j)_j\|_{\ell_2}$ and $\|(v(x), 0, 0, \dots)\|_{\ell_2} = |v(x)|$
(\Cref{lem:lq-basic}).
\end{proof}

\section{The strong type of vector-valued singular integrals}
\label{sec:vector-valued-strong-type}

Let $(\theta_j)_{j \in \N}$ be a Calder\'on--Zygmund family on $V$ with overlap $B$ and
H\"ormander constant $H$ (\Cref{def:cz-family}). This section proves, for every
$1 < p < \infty$, the strong type $(p, p)$ of the analysis operator
$f \mapsto \|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}$ and of the synthesis operators
$(g_j)_j \mapsto \sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j$ for finite sets $s \subseteq \N$, with explicit
constants. For $p = 2$ these are the Plancherel bounds. For $1 < p < 2$ Marcinkiewicz
interpolation between the weak type $(1,1)$ of \Cref{thm:vector-valued-weak-type} and the
$L_2$ bounds applies: to the analysis operator in the form of the formalisation of Carleson's
theorem (\Cref{thm:marcinkiewicz-interpolation}), and to the synthesis operators in the form
for an abstract input type (\Cref{thm:marcinkiewicz-abstract}), whose inputs are families of
measurable functions. For $2 < p < \infty$, the adjoint identity exchanges the two operators of
the adjoint family $\theta_j^*(x) = \overline{\theta_j(-x)}$, which has the same overlap and
H\"ormander constant, at the conjugate exponent $p' < 2$, and \Cref{thm:lp-norm-duality}
returns to $L_p$. These are the classical $L_p$ bounds of vector-valued singular
integrals~\cite{BenedekCalderonPanzone}; see also Stein~\cite{SteinSingular}.

\begin{theorem}[The strong type $(2,2)$]
\label{thm:cz-strong-type-two}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.hasStrongType_lqNorm_conv_two, Rd.IsCZFamily.eLpNorm_lqNorm_conv_two_le,
  Rd.IsCZFamily.eLpNorm_sum_conv_two_le}
\leanok
\uses{cor:cz-family-l2-bounds, lem:lp-norm-from-power-integrals, def:weak-type-operators,
  lem:lp-norm-nonnegative}
For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$, every Calder\'on--Zygmund family $(\theta_j)_j$ on $V$ with
overlap $B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$, every $f \in L_2(V)$, every finite set
$s \subseteq \N$ and all $g_j \in L_2(V)$,
\[
  \bigl\| \|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_2 \leq B^{1/2} \|f\|_2 , \qquad
  \Bigl\| \sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j \Bigr\|_2
  \leq B^{1/2} \bigl\| \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_2 .
\]
In particular the analysis operator has strong type $(2, 2)$ with constant $B^{1/2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The function $x \mapsto \|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}$ is almost everywhere measurable
(\Cref{lem:lp-norm-nonnegative}). \Cref{lem:lp-norm-from-power-integrals} with $p = 2$ and
$C = B$ turns the integral bounds of \Cref{cor:cz-family-l2-bounds} into the norm bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Subadditivity and weak type $(1,1)$ of the analysis operator]
\label{lem:analysis-subadditive-weak-type}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.aeSubadditiveOn_lqNorm_conv, Rd.IsCZFamily.hasWeakType_lqNorm_conv}
\leanok
\uses{def:cz-family, lem:conv-assoc, lem:lq-basic, thm:vector-valued-weak-type,
  def:weak-type-operators, def:vector-weak-const, lem:distribution-weak-norm-basic}
For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$ and every Calder\'on--Zygmund family $(\theta_j)_j$ on $V$ with
overlap $B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$, the analysis operator
$f \mapsto \|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}$ is almost everywhere subadditive with constant
$1$ on the functions in $L_1(V)$ or $L_2(V)$. If $n \geq 1$, it has weak type $(1, 1)$ with
constant $C_V(B, H)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
For $f \in L_p(V)$ and $g \in L_r(V)$ with $p, r \in \{1, 2\}$,
$\theta_j * (f + g) = \theta_j * f + \theta_j * g$ almost everywhere for every $j$
(\Cref{lem:conv-assoc}), and Minkowski's inequality in $\ell_2$ (\Cref{lem:lq-basic}) gives the
subadditivity. For $t > 0$, \Cref{thm:vector-valued-weak-type} gives
$t \, |\{\|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} > t\}| \leq C_V(B, H) \int |f|$, and for $t = 0$
the left side vanishes; the supremum over $t$ is the weak $L_1$ norm
(\Cref{lem:distribution-weak-norm-basic}).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The strong type constant below $2$]
\label{def:cz-const-below}
\lean{Rd.czConstBelow, Rd.czConstBelow_ne_top}
\leanok
\uses{def:marcinkiewicz-const, def:vector-weak-const}
For $1 < p < 2$ and $B, H \in [0, \infty]$,
\[
  S^-_{V,p}(B, H) = C^{\mathrm M}_p\bigl(C_V(B, H), B\bigr)^{1/p} .
\]
It is finite if $B$ and $H$ are.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The analysis operator for $1 < p < 2$]
\label{thm:cz-analysis-below-two}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.hasStrongType_lqNorm_conv_of_lt, Rd.IsCZFamily.eLpNorm_lqNorm_conv_le_of_lt}
\leanok
\uses{thm:marcinkiewicz-interpolation, lem:analysis-subadditive-weak-type,
  thm:cz-strong-type-two, def:cz-const-below}
Let $n \geq 1$ and $1 < p < 2$. For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$ and every Calder\'on--Zygmund
family $(\theta_j)_j$ on $V$ with overlap $B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$, the analysis
operator has strong type $(p, p)$ with constant $S^-_{V,p}(B, H)$: for every $f \in L_p(V)$,
\[
  \bigl\| \|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_p \leq S^-_{V,p}(B, H) \, \|f\|_p .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
\Cref{thm:marcinkiewicz-interpolation} applies with $A = 1$, $C_1 = C_V(B, H)$ and
$C_2 = B^{1/2}$ (\Cref{lem:analysis-subadditive-weak-type}, \Cref{thm:cz-strong-type-two}), and
$N_p(1, C_V(B, H), B^{1/2}) = S^-_{V,p}(B, H)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The synthesis operators for $1 < p < 2$]
\label{thm:cz-synthesis-below-two}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.eLpNorm_sum_conv_le_of_lt_of_measurable,
  Rd.IsCZFamily.eLpNorm_sum_conv_le_of_lt}
\leanok
\uses{thm:marcinkiewicz-abstract, thm:vector-valued-weak-type, cor:cz-family-l2-bounds,
  lem:finite-families-lp-l2, lem:fefferman-stein-split, lem:conv-assoc, def:conv,
  def:cz-const-below}
Let $n \geq 1$ and $1 < p < 2$. For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$, every Calder\'on--Zygmund family
$(\theta_j)_j$ on $V$ with overlap $B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$, every finite set
$s \subseteq \N$ and all $g_j \in L_p(V)$, $j \in \N$,
\[
  \Bigl\| \sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j \Bigr\|_p
  \leq S^-_{V,p}(B, H) \, \bigl\| \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_p .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
First let every $g_j$ be measurable with
$\bigl\| \|(g_j)_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_p < \infty$. Apply \Cref{thm:marcinkiewicz-abstract} to
the families of measurable functions, with the size $G_g = \|(g_j)_j\|_{\ell_2}$, the
restriction $g|_S = (\mathbf 1_S g_j)_j$, whose size is $\mathbf 1_S G_g$
(\Cref{lem:fefferman-stein-split}), and
$T g = \bigl|\sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j\bigr|$. If $\int G_g^p < \infty$, every $g_j$ lies in
$L_p(V)$ (\Cref{lem:finite-families-lp-l2}), so convolution is additive almost everywhere
(\Cref{lem:conv-assoc}) and $T g \leq T(g|_S) + T(g|_{V \setminus S})$.
\Cref{thm:vector-valued-weak-type} gives the weak bound with $C_1 = C_V(B, H)$ and
\Cref{cor:cz-family-l2-bounds} the $L_2$ bound with $C_2 = B$. In general, replace $g_j$ by a
measurable function equal to it almost everywhere for $j \in s$ and by $0$ for $j \notin s$: the
sum is unchanged (\Cref{def:conv}), the right side can only decrease, and it becomes finite
(\Cref{lem:finite-families-lp-l2}).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Pairings through the adjoint family]
\label{lem:cz-pairings-adjoint}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.enorm_sum_integral_conv_mul_conj_le,
  Rd.IsCZFamily.enorm_integral_sum_conv_mul_conj_le}
\leanok
\uses{cor:convolution-adjoint-conj, lem:cz-family-adjoint, thm:cz-analysis-below-two,
  thm:cz-synthesis-below-two, lem:holder-lp-norms, lem:lq-cauchy-schwarz-sequences,
  thm:young}
Let $n \geq 1$, $1 < q < 2$ and $p = q/(q - 1)$. For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$, every
Calder\'on--Zygmund family $(\theta_j)_j$ on $V$ with overlap $B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$
and every finite set $s \subseteq \N$: for every $f \in L_p(V)$ and all $g_j \in L_q(V)$,
\[
  \Bigl| \sum_{j \in s} \int_V (\theta_j * f) \, \overline{g_j} \Bigr|
  \leq S^-_{V,q}(B, H) \, \|f\|_p \, \bigl\| \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_q ,
\]
and for all $g_j \in L_p(V)$ and every $u \in L_q(V)$,
\[
  \Bigl| \int_V \Bigl(\sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j\Bigr) \overline u \Bigr|
  \leq S^-_{V,q}(B, H) \, \bigl\| \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_p \, \|u\|_q .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
By \Cref{cor:convolution-adjoint-conj}, every pairing moves $\theta_j$ to the other factor as
$\theta_j^*$, and $(\theta_j^*)_j$ is a Calder\'on--Zygmund family with overlap $B$ and
H\"ormander constant $H$ (\Cref{lem:cz-family-adjoint}). The first pairing becomes
$\int_V f \, \overline{\sum_{j \in s} \theta_j^* * g_j}$, and H\"older's inequality
(\Cref{lem:holder-lp-norms}) and \Cref{thm:cz-synthesis-below-two} for the adjoint family
at $q$ bound it. The second becomes
$\sum_{j \in s} \int_V g_j \, \overline{\theta_j^* * u}$; the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality at
every point (\Cref{lem:lq-cauchy-schwarz-sequences}), H\"older's inequality and
\Cref{thm:cz-analysis-below-two} for the adjoint family at $q$ bound it.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The strong type for $2 < p < \infty$]
\label{thm:cz-above-two}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.eLpNorm_lqNorm_conv_le_of_two_lt, Rd.IsCZFamily.eLpNorm_sum_conv_le_of_two_lt}
\leanok
\uses{lem:cz-pairings-adjoint, thm:lp-norm-duality, lem:countable-minkowski, thm:young,
  lem:cancel-conjugate-power, lem:lp-series-minkowski, def:cz-const-below}
Let $n \geq 1$, $2 < p < \infty$ and $p' = p/(p - 1)$. For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$ and every
Calder\'on--Zygmund family $(\theta_j)_j$ on $V$ with overlap $B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$:
for every $f \in L_p(V)$,
\[
  \bigl\| \|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_p \leq S^-_{V,p'}(B, H) \, \|f\|_p ,
\]
and for every finite set $s \subseteq \N$ and all $g_j \in L_p(V)$,
\[
  \Bigl\| \sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j \Bigr\|_p
  \leq S^-_{V,p'}(B, H) \, \bigl\| \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_p .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
By \Cref{lem:cancel-conjugate-power}, $1 < p' < 2$. For every $J \in \N$, the family
$u_j = \theta_j * f$ for $j < J$ and $u_j = 0$ for $j \geq J$ lies in $L_p(V)$
(\Cref{thm:young}), and the first bound of \Cref{lem:cz-pairings-adjoint} is the hypothesis of
\Cref{thm:lp-norm-duality} with $A = S^-_{V,p'}(B, H) \|f\|_p$. The truncated $\ell_2$ norms
increase to $\|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}$ (\Cref{lem:countable-minkowski}), and monotone
convergence in $L_p$ (\Cref{lem:lp-series-minkowski}) gives the first inequality. The second
is \Cref{thm:lp-norm-duality} for
$v = \sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j \in L_p(V)$ (\Cref{thm:young}) with the second bound of
\Cref{lem:cz-pairings-adjoint}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The strong type constant]
\label{def:cz-const}
\lean{Rd.czConst, Rd.czConst_ne_top}
\leanok
\uses{def:cz-const-below}
For $1 < p < \infty$ and $B, H \in [0, \infty]$,
\[
  S_{V,p}(B, H) =
  \begin{cases}
    S^-_{V,p}(B, H) & \text{for } p < 2, \\
    B^{1/2} & \text{for } p = 2, \\
    S^-_{V,p/(p-1)}(B, H) & \text{for } p > 2 .
  \end{cases}
\]
It is finite if $B$ and $H$ are.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The strong type of vector-valued singular integrals]
\label{thm:vector-valued-strong-type}
\lean{Rd.IsCZFamily.eLpNorm_lqNorm_conv_le, Rd.IsCZFamily.eLpNorm_sum_conv_le}
\leanok
\uses{thm:cz-strong-type-two, thm:cz-analysis-below-two, thm:cz-synthesis-below-two,
  thm:cz-above-two, def:cz-const}
Let $n \geq 1$ and $1 < p < \infty$. For all $B, H \in [0, \infty]$, every
Calder\'on--Zygmund family $(\theta_j)_j$ on $V$ with overlap $B$ and H\"ormander constant $H$,
every $f \in L_p(V)$, every finite set $s \subseteq \N$ and all $g_j \in L_p(V)$,
\[
  \bigl\| \|((\theta_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_p \leq S_{V,p}(B, H) \, \|f\|_p
\]
and
\[
  \Bigl\| \sum_{j \in s} \theta_j * g_j \Bigr\|_p
  \leq S_{V,p}(B, H) \, \bigl\| \|(g_j(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_p .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
\Cref{thm:cz-analysis-below-two} and \Cref{thm:cz-synthesis-below-two} for $p < 2$,
\Cref{thm:cz-strong-type-two} for $p = 2$, and \Cref{thm:cz-above-two} for $p > 2$.
\end{proof}

\section{The square function theorem}
\label{sec:square-function}

For $f \in L_p(V)$ the square function $x \mapsto \|((\psi_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2}$ collects the
Littlewood--Paley blocks at every point, and its $L_p$ norm is $\|f\|_{\TL{0}{p}{2}}$. The square
function theorem says that this norm is equivalent to $\|f\|_p$ for $1 < p < \infty$, so
$\TL{0}{p}{2} = L_p(V)$. The upper bound is the strong type of the analysis operator of the
Calder\'on--Zygmund family $(\psi_j)_j$; the lower bound combines the reproducing formula
$\sum_{j < J} \tilde\psi_j * (\psi_j * f) \to f$ with the strong type of the synthesis
operators of the family $(\tilde\psi_j)_j$ (\Cref{thm:vector-valued-strong-type}). Stein's
book~\cite{SteinSingular} proves the Littlewood--Paley theorem through vector-valued singular
integrals, with the lower bound by duality, and Triebel~\cite{Triebel} states it as
$\TL{0}{p}{2} = L_p(V)$. Grafakos~\cite{Grafakos} gives a textbook account of the
Littlewood--Paley theorem and of vector-valued singular integrals.

\begin{definition}[The square function constants]
\label{def:square-function-consts}
\lean{Rd.squareFunctionConst, Rd.squareFunctionConst_ne_top, Rd.squareSynthesisConst,
  Rd.squareSynthesisConst_ne_top}
\leanok
\uses{def:cz-const, def:hormander-const, def:psi-base, def:psi-dual}
For $1 < p < \infty$,
\[
  Q_{V,p} = S_{V,p}\bigl(2, 4 H_{A^{\psi}}\bigr) , \qquad
  \tilde Q_{V,p} = S_{V,p}\bigl(4, 4 H_{\tilde A}\bigr) .
\]
Both are finite.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The upper square function bound]
\label{thm:square-function-upper}
\lean{Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_zero_two_eq, Rd.triebelLizorkinNorm_zero_two_le,
  Rd.memTriebelLizorkin_zero_two}
\leanok
\uses{def:triebel-lizorkin, prop:tl-elementary, thm:cz-family-psi,
  thm:vector-valued-strong-type, def:square-function-consts}
For every $1 \leq p < \infty$ and every $f \in L_p(V)$,
\[
  \|f\|_{\TL{0}{p}{2}} = \bigl\| \|((\psi_j * f)(x))_j\|_{\ell_2} \bigr\|_p .
\]
If moreover $n \geq 1$ and $1 < p < \infty$, then
\[
  \|f\|_{\TL{0}{p}{2}} \leq Q_{V,p} \, \|f\|_p ,
\]
and in particular $f \in \TL{0}{p}{2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The equality is the case $q = 2$ of \Cref{prop:tl-elementary}. The blocks form a
Calder\'on--Zygmund family with overlap $2$ and H\"ormander constant $4 H_{A^{\psi}}$
(\Cref{thm:cz-family-psi}), and \Cref{thm:vector-valued-strong-type} bounds its analysis
operator.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The reproducing formula]
\label{lem:square-function-reproducing}
\lean{Rd.conv_psiDual_blockFun_ae, Rd.sum_conv_psiDual_blockFun_ae,
  Rd.tendsto_eLpNorm_sum_conv_psiDual_blockFun_sub}
\leanok
\uses{def:triebel-lizorkin, lem:conv-assoc, lem:psi-dual-reproduces, lem:lp-blocks,
  lem:lp-kernels-basic, lem:psi-dual-basic}
Let $1 \leq p < \infty$ and $f \in L_p(V)$. For every $j \in \N$,
$\tilde\psi_j * (\psi_j * f) = \psi_j * f$ almost everywhere. For every finite set
$s \subseteq \N$,
\[
  \sum_{j \in s} \tilde\psi_j * (\psi_j * f) = \sum_{j \in s} \Delta_j f
\]
almost everywhere, and $\sum_{j < J} \tilde\psi_j * (\psi_j * f) \to f$ in $L_p(V)$ as
$J \to \infty$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\leanok
The kernels $\psi_j$ and $\tilde\psi_j$ are integrable (\Cref{lem:lp-kernels-basic},
\Cref{lem:psi-dual-basic}). By associativity (\Cref{lem:conv-assoc}) and
$\tilde\psi_j * \psi_j = \psi_j$ (\Cref{lem:psi-dual-reproduces}),
$\tilde\psi_j * (\psi_j * f) = (\tilde\psi_j * \psi_j) * f = \psi_j * f$ almost everywhere, and
$\psi_j * f$ represents $\Delta_j f$ (\Cref{def:triebel-lizorkin}). The partial sums
$\sum_{j < J} \Delta_j f$ tend to $f$ in $L_p(V)$ (\Cref{lem:lp-blocks}).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The lower square function bound]
\label{thm:square-function-lower}
\lean{Rd.enorm_le_triebelLizorkinNorm_zero_two}
\leanok
\uses{lem:square-function-reproducing, thm:cz-family-psi-dual, thm:vector-valued-strong-type,
